questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: An eschar at the site of a mite bite with fever, lymphadenopathy and raised transaminases in a rice-field worker suggests:
questions.concept: Orientia tsutsugamushi is inoculated by trombiculid mite larvae and the painless necrotic eschar with regional nodes is the single most useful clinical clue.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The drug of choice for scrub typhus is:
questions.concept: Rickettsiae are obligate intracellular organisms, so cell-penetrating agents such as doxycycline or azithromycin work while beta-lactams are useless; defervescence within 48 hours supports the diagnosis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Conjunctival suffusion with jaundice, renal failure and myalgia after wading through floodwater indicates:
questions.concept: Leptospires penetrate abraded skin and mucosa from rodent urine, and the combination of hepatic and renal involvement with severe calf tenderness is characteristic.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The most useful confirmatory test for leptospirosis in the second week of illness is:
options: Microscopic agglutination test on paired sera
questions.concept: Leptospiraemia is confined to the first week while antibodies appear in the second, so serology with a fourfold rise is the practical reference standard.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The characteristic renal lesion of leptospirosis is:
options: Non-oliguric hypokalaemic acute kidney injury from tubulointerstitial nephritis
questions.concept: Direct tubular injury impairs sodium and potassium handling, so unlike most causes of acute kidney injury urine output is preserved and potassium is low.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Undulant fever, sacroiliitis and hepatosplenomegaly in a person consuming unpasteurised milk suggests:
questions.concept: Brucella is a facultative intracellular organism requiring prolonged combination therapy with doxycycline and either streptomycin or rifampicin to prevent relapse.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Indian tick typhus caused by Rickettsia conorii characteristically produces:
options: A maculopapular rash involving palms and soles with a tache noire
questions.concept: The vasculitic rash of spotted fever group rickettsiae involves the extremities including palms and soles, which distinguishes it from typhus group infections.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Thrombocytopenia with a normal or low white count, raised transaminases and a negative dengue NS1 in a patient with an eschar should prompt:
options: Empirical doxycycline for scrub typhus while awaiting IgM ELISA
questions.concept: Untreated scrub typhus progresses to acute respiratory distress syndrome, myocarditis and meningoencephalitis, and mortality falls sharply with early empirical doxycycline in endemic settings.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction after starting penicillin in leptospirosis is due to:
options: Massive release of spirochaetal antigen triggering cytokine surge
questions.concept: Rapid killing releases lipoproteins that provoke fever, rigors and hypotension within hours, and it is managed supportively rather than by stopping the antibiotic.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The Philadelphia chromosome in chronic myeloid leukaemia results from:
questions.concept: The fusion gene encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase, which is precisely why imatinib and later tyrosine kinase inhibitors transformed the prognosis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Bone pain, anaemia, renal failure and hypercalcaemia in an older adult should prompt evaluation for:
questions.concept: Clonal plasma cells produce a paraprotein and activate osteoclasts, giving the CRAB features that define symptomatic disease requiring treatment.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Painless cervical lymphadenopathy with pain after alcohol and Reed-Sternberg cells indicates:
questions.concept: Hodgkin disease spreads contiguously through nodal groups, which is why staging and radiotherapy planning differ from the multicentric spread of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Disseminated intravascular coagulation at presentation is most characteristic of which leukaemia:
questions.concept: Granule procoagulants released from abnormal promyelocytes trigger consumptive coagulopathy, and all-trans retinoic acid is started on suspicion before cytogenetics return.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Smudge cells on the peripheral smear with absolute lymphocytosis in an elderly patient indicate:
questions.concept: Fragile mature B lymphocytes rupture during smear preparation, and flow cytometry showing CD5 and CD23 co-expression confirms the clone.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Tumour lysis syndrome is characterised by:
questions.concept: Rapid cell death releases intracellular contents; phosphate binds calcium and precipitates in tubules, so hydration with rasburicase or allopurinol is given prophylactically.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance is distinguished from myeloma by:
options: Paraprotein under 3 g/dL, marrow plasma cells under 10 percent and no end-organ damage
questions.concept: It progresses to myeloma at about 1 percent per year, so it needs surveillance rather than chemotherapy.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A starry-sky appearance on lymph node biopsy with a translocation involving MYC indicates:
questions.concept: Tingible-body macrophages among sheets of proliferating cells give the pattern, the proliferation index approaches 100 percent, and it is one of the fastest growing but most curable human tumours.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The single best initial investigation in suspected multiple myeloma with normal serum electrophoresis is:
questions.concept: Light chain only myeloma produces no detectable heavy chain band, and light chains are cleared renally so serum electrophoresis misses them while the free light chain ratio detects them.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The cardinal triad of Parkinson disease is:
questions.concept: Bradykinesia is obligatory for the diagnosis, and the pathology is loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta with Lewy bodies.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The most effective symptomatic drug in Parkinson disease is:
questions.concept: Peripheral decarboxylase inhibition allows more levodopa to reach the brain and reduces nausea, and no other agent matches its effect on bradykinesia and rigidity.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Early prominent visual hallucinations with fluctuating cognition and parkinsonism suggest:
questions.concept: Marked neuroleptic sensitivity is a further clue, and antipsychotics can cause severe irreversible deterioration in these patients.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A young adult with tremor, dysarthria, Kayser-Fleischer rings and deranged liver function has:
questions.concept: Impaired biliary copper excretion from ATP7B mutation deposits copper in liver, basal ganglia and cornea, and treatment is chelation with penicillamine or trientine plus zinc.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Progressive dementia with early personality change, disinhibition and preserved memory suggests:
questions.concept: Behavioural variant disease begins in the frontal and anterior temporal lobes, so social conduct fails long before episodic memory does.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The triad of gait apraxia, urinary incontinence and dementia with ventriculomegaly indicates:
questions.concept: It is one of the few reversible dementias, and improvement in gait after a high-volume lumbar tap predicts benefit from ventriculoperitoneal shunting.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Chorea with progressive dementia and a positive family history of autosomal dominant inheritance indicates:
questions.concept: CAG trinucleotide expansion in the huntingtin gene shows anticipation, and caudate atrophy widens the frontal horns on imaging.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Parkinsonism with early falls and vertical supranuclear gaze palsy suggests:
questions.concept: Poor levodopa response, axial rigidity and downgaze restriction with midbrain atrophy on MRI distinguish this tauopathy from idiopathic disease.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Parkinsonism with early severe autonomic failure and cerebellar signs indicates:
questions.concept: Alpha-synuclein inclusions in glia affect striatonigral, olivopontocerebellar and autonomic pathways, giving orthostatic hypotension and urinary failure early in the course.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Gower sign in a boy with calf pseudohypertrophy indicates:
options: Proximal muscle weakness of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
questions.concept: The child climbs up his own thighs because hip and knee extensors are too weak to straighten the trunk directly, and creatine kinase is grossly elevated.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A woman whose brother has Duchenne muscular dystrophy asks about risk to her sons. The expected risk if she is a carrier is:
options: One in two of her sons affected
One in four of all children affected regardless of sex
questions.concept: The dystrophin gene lies at Xp21, so a carrier mother transmits the mutant X to half her sons, who are affected, and to half her daughters, who become carriers.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Fatigable ptosis and diplopia worsening through the day indicate:
questions.concept: Antibodies to the postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor reduce endplate potentials, so repeated use exhausts transmission and rest restores it.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation at low frequency is characteristic of:
questions.concept: Postsynaptic receptor loss makes successive endplate potentials fall below threshold, whereas presynaptic disorders show an incremental response after brief exercise.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A patient with myasthenia develops respiratory failure. The immediate priority is:
options: Airway support with plasma exchange or intravenous immunoglobulin
questions.concept: Rapid-acting immunotherapy plus ventilatory support treats the crisis; more anticholinesterase risks cholinergic crisis and steroid-sparing agents take months to act.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Proximal weakness with a heliotrope rash and Gottron papules indicates:
questions.concept: It is a complement-mediated microangiopathy with perifascicular atrophy, and in adults it carries a significant association with underlying malignancy.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Asymmetric distal weakness with fasciculations and brisk reflexes without sensory loss suggests:
questions.concept: Combined upper and lower motor neuron signs in the same region with intact sensation is the hallmark, and riluzole gives a modest survival benefit.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Grip myotonia, frontal balding, cataract and cardiac conduction defects indicate:
questions.concept: A CTG expansion in the DMPK gene affects multiple systems, and the conduction disease can cause sudden death, so annual electrocardiography is essential.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Proximal weakness that improves briefly after exercise, with autonomic dryness and an underlying small cell lung cancer, indicates:
questions.concept: Antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels reduce acetylcholine release, and brief maximal contraction facilitates calcium entry, giving post-exercise improvement.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Confusion, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia in a chronic alcoholic indicate:
questions.concept: Thiamine must be given before any glucose load because carbohydrate metabolism consumes the remaining thiamine and can precipitate irreversible Korsakoff psychosis.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs and bleeding gums indicate deficiency of:
questions.concept: Ascorbate is the cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase in collagen synthesis, so defective collagen weakens vessel walls and impairs wound healing.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia in a maize-eating population indicate deficiency of:
questions.concept: Maize niacin is bound and its tryptophan content is low, and Casal necklace is the classic photosensitive dermatitis of pellagra.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Night blindness with Bitot spots and conjunctival xerosis indicate deficiency of:
questions.concept: Retinal is required to regenerate rhodopsin and retinoic acid maintains mucosal differentiation, so both dark adaptation and epithelial integrity fail.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: A malnourished patient on antitubercular therapy develops burning feet and glove-and-stocking sensory loss after two months. The deficiency responsible is:
questions.concept: Isoniazid forms a hydrazone with pyridoxal phosphate and increases its urinary loss, so 10 to 25 mg of pyridoxine daily is given prophylactically to those at risk.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Refeeding syndrome after starting nutrition in a severely malnourished patient is characterised by:
questions.concept: Insulin release drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly for ATP synthesis, which can cause fatal arrhythmias unless calories are increased slowly with electrolyte monitoring.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Angular stomatitis, glossitis and normocytic anaemia after prolonged phenytoin therapy suggests deficiency of:
questions.concept: Phenytoin impairs folate absorption and induces its metabolism, which is also why the drug can precipitate megaloblastic change and worsen seizure control in a vicious cycle.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Selenium deficiency is classically associated with:
questions.concept: Selenium is required for glutathione peroxidase, and its deficiency in low-selenium soil regions of China produced an endemic congestive cardiomyopathy.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: Nutritional & vitamin deficiency states in adults
questions.stem: Diarrhoea, alopecia and a perioral and acral vesiculobullous rash after prolonged parenteral nutrition indicate deficiency of:
questions.concept: Zinc is essential for many metalloenzymes and for epithelial turnover, and the picture resembles the inherited acrodermatitis enteropathica.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 331 (Vitamin and Trace Mineral Deficiency)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: The body mass index cut-off defining obesity for Asian Indians is:
questions.concept: Indians develop visceral adiposity and insulin resistance at a lower body mass index, so the consensus guidelines lower both the overweight and obesity thresholds.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A man with central obesity and impaired fasting glucose has triglycerides of 280 mg/dL, HDL of 32 mg/dL and an LDL of 110 mg/dL. This pattern is termed:
options: Atherogenic dyslipidaemia of the metabolic syndrome
questions.concept: Excess free fatty acid flux drives hepatic VLDL output and cholesteryl ester transfer remodels HDL and LDL into small dense particles, so the LDL number understates the risk.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with established coronary artery disease has an LDL of 150 mg/dL despite diet. The agent that will most reduce his risk of further events is:
questions.concept: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, and only statins have consistent secondary-prevention outcome evidence at this level of risk.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Tendon xanthomata with an LDL above 190 mg/dL and a strong family history of early coronary disease indicate:
questions.concept: LDL receptor mutations are usually autosomal dominant, and cascade screening of relatives with early high-intensity statin therapy is the key intervention.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A fasting triglyceride level above 885 mg/dL primarily risks:
questions.concept: Chylomicronaemia releases free fatty acids in pancreatic capillaries causing inflammation, so fibrates, dietary fat restriction and control of diabetes take priority over LDL lowering.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Statin therapy should be temporarily stopped if creatine kinase rises above:
options: Ten times the upper limit of normal with muscle symptoms
questions.concept: Mild elevations are common and benign, but marked elevation with symptoms risks rhabdomyolysis, and interacting drugs such as macrolides, azoles and fibrates increase that risk.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: An Asian Indian man with a body mass index of 34 and poorly controlled type 2 diabetes despite three agents is being considered for metabolic surgery. He:
options: Meets the Indian consensus threshold, since comorbidity lowers it to 32.5
Does not qualify until his body mass index exceeds 40
Qualifies only if he is above 45
Should never be offered surgery with diabetes
questions.concept: Indian thresholds are set lower than Western ones because visceral adiposity and insulin resistance appear at a lower body mass index, and diabetes remission is a principal indication.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Which lipid-lowering agent works by inhibiting the intestinal sterol transporter NPC1L1:
questions.concept: Blocking cholesterol absorption lowers LDL by about 20 percent and adds to statin effect, as shown in the IMPROVE-IT trial.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A patient with familial hypercholesterolaemia remains at an LDL of 160 mg/dL on maximal statin and ezetimibe. Adding evolocumab lowers LDL because it:
options: Prevents lysosomal degradation of recycled hepatic LDL receptors
Binds bile acids in the gut
questions.concept: PCSK9 normally escorts the internalised receptor to the lysosome, so blocking it increases receptor density on the hepatocyte surface and clearance of circulating LDL.
questions.reference: Harrison 21e, Ch. 407 (Obesity) and Ch. 407 (Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism)
